display_name: Acacius, companion of Patrick of Prusa

names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Μαΐου, «Άγιοι Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας, Ακάκιος, Μένανδρος και Πολύαινος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the heading of the Охридски пролог’s first entry for 19. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученик Патрикије епископ бруски, са три презвитера: Акакијем, Менандром и Полиеном.“ — Свети is not a rank and презвитер is the `presbyter` this batch adds to `types`. Measured before drafting with `foldchk.py`: `[('acacius-of-melitene', 'sr'), ('acacius-the-centurion', 'sr'), ('acacius-the-kausokalyvite', 'sr')]`, so the fold is four wide and is read in this batch’s commit message. **THE HEADING PRINTS THE NAME IN THE INSTRUMENTAL AND THE NOMINATIVE IS RESTORED, WHICH IS A READING AND IS SAID HERE.** „са три презвитера: Акакијем, Менандром и Полиеном“ governs the instrumental, and the body names none of the three at all, so no nominative is printed anywhere on the page. **The restoration is grammar and not transliteration**, and for each of the three it is unique: Акакијем → Акакије, the form three other folders already hold off this same book; Полиеном → Полиен, the form `polyaenus-of-rome` already holds in Russian; and Менандром → Менандар and not Менандер, because an -ар stem drops its a before the instrumental ending while an -ер stem does not, which would have given Менандером. **This is the one place in five days where a stored form is not a string copied off the page**, and it is flagged rather than passed over.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας, Ακάκιος, Μένανδρος και Πολύαινος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives the four of them one narrative under Patrick's name. The corpus already keeps `patrick-of-prusa` from doxologia.ro's 19 mai and its Romanian line names him alone; these three fellow-workers are not in the corpus under any name, and none of its men called Acacius, Menander or Polyaenus is a companion of Patrick — `polyaenus-of-rome` is the martyr kept with Hermas and Serapion at Rome. The page gives the four no year and no emperor, only the governor Julian the Consular, so there is no `dates` object. The apolytikion calls all four «Ἱεραρχῶν ἱερῶν», holy hierarchs, which the prose does not: the prose calls the three συνεργάται, fellow-workers, and no rank beyond martyr is recorded here.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.06.2026 (19. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученик Патрикије епископ бруски, са три презвитера: Акакијем, Менандром и Полиеном.“

attestations.note: One of the three presbyters of the day’s first entry, **named in its heading and nowhere else in it** — the body speaks of them only as „осталој тројици његових презвитера“ and „незлобиви ови следбеници Христови“. **This is the first Serbian row this folder has had, and the second calendar of any kind to keep him**: the Romanian and Russian rows are `undocumented` and only the Greek was venerated, on the same menologion 19/5. **`presbyter` IS ADDED to `types`.** „са три презвитера“ is the Prologue’s own word for the three, and BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §5 maps Презвитер → presbyter; doxologia’s life calls them „three of his priests“ and saint.gr only „fellow-workers“, so this book is where the order is stated plainly. **It changes nothing in print**: `presbyter` is absent from `PRECEDENCE` in `src/lib/honorific.js`, so `martyr` still composes the rank and the word reaches the reader only in the saint page’s facts line — the same ground on which `wonderworker` was added to `achillius-of-larissa` on 15 May and `monk` refused to `nicholas-the-mystikos` on 16 May. **THREE BOOKS, THREE NAMES FOR THE GOVERNOR, AND A FOURTH NAME THAT MAY BE THE SAME MAN PROMOTED TO EMPEROR.** doxologia calls him **Julius**, governor of Bithynia; saint.gr calls him **Julian the Consular**; this book calls him **Јуније**, Junius, „намесник царски“, the imperial deputy. **And this book alone names an emperor** — Julian the Apostate — which neither of the others does. **Whether the Prologue has read saint.gr’s governor Julian as the emperor Julian, or dates the martyrdom to that reign on its own authority, cannot be told from the page**, and nothing is decided on it here: no year is taken from the reign, no name is corrected, and all three readings are in the prose. **That is the reading of this entry and it is the author’s if it is to be resolved.** **NO YEAR, AND THE REFUSAL IS THIS WAVE’S STANDING ONE.** „Пострадали за веру Христову у време Јулијана Одступника“ names a reign and **gives it no bounds**, so nothing is built on it — as „У време царовања Декијева“ was refused for `isidore-of-chios` on 14 May and „У време Декијево“ for the three Athenians on 18 May. **All four folders of this company still carry no `dates` object**, and no calendar read for any of them has given one. **THREE `related` ROWS ADDED.** This folder and its three companions all carried **`related: None`**; the entry narrates the four as one company beheaded together, so each now relates the other three. No `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Τετράς θεοφόρητος, Ἱεραρχῶν ἱερῶν, Τριάδα τὴν ἂκτιστον, κατ’ ἐναντίον ἐχθρῶν, πανσόφως ἐκήρυξε, Πατρίκιος ὁ τῆς Προύσης, θεηγόρος ποιμάντωρ, Ἀκάκιος σὺν Μενάνδρῳ, καὶ Πολύαινος ἃμα· διὸ καὶ ὡς ἀθλήσαντες, δόξης ἠξιώθησαν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε, on the page of «Άγιος Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας»

english.text: A God-bearing four of holy hierarchs preached the uncreated Trinity in all wisdom in the face of their enemies: Patrick, the God-speaking shepherd of Prusa, Acacius together with Menander, and Polyaenus with them; and so, having contended, they were counted worthy of glory.

hymns.text: Οἱ Μάρτυρες σου Κύριε, ἐν τῇ ἀθλήσει αὐτῶν, τὸ στέφος ἐκομίσαντο τῆς ἀφθαρσίας, ἐκ σοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν· σχόντες γὰρ τὴν ἰσχύν σου, τοὺς τυράννους καθεῖλον· ἔθραυσαν καὶ δαιμόνων τὰ ἀνίσχυρα θράση. Αὐτῶν ταῖς ἱκεσίαις Χριστὲ ὁ Θεός, σῶσον τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχύ προκατάλαβε, on the page of «Άγιος Πατρίκιος επίσκοπος Προύσας» — the common of martyrs

english.text: Your martyrs, O Lord, in their contest received the crown of incorruption from you, our God; for having your strength they brought the tyrants down, and shattered the powerless insolence of the demons. At their entreaties, Christ God, save our souls.
